1000599.etyen:
From ekvatorial (“equatorial”) + Guinea (“Guinea”). The territory was formerly known in Norwegian as Spansk Guinea (“Spanish Guinea”) and became independent in 1968 under the present name. Compare Spanish Guinea Ecuatorial (“Equatorial Guinea”), the country's principal official-language name.
The first element ekvatorial (“equatorial”) is a borrowing; compare German äquatorial, ultimately from Latin aequator (“equalizer; equator”). It refers to the country's location near the equator, although no part of Ekvatorial-Guinea actually lies on the equator.
Ultimate origin of the Guinea element unce

1001111.etyen:
Derived from Latin Rebecca, from Ancient Greek Ῥεβέκκα (Rhebékka), ultimately from Biblical Hebrew רִבְקָה (Rivqā). The meaning and deeper origin of the Hebrew name are uncertain; it may ultimately be of Aramaic origin. The name was spread through the biblical Rebecca, the wife of Isaac and mother of Jacob and Esau. First attested in the 17th century in Norway.
Cognate with Norwegian Nynorsk Rebekka, Danish Rebekka, Swedish Rebecka, Icelandic Rebekka, Faroese Rebekka, German Rebekka, Finnish Rebekka and English Rebecca.
